record.name: Dane County Minor Home Repair Program
record.administeredBy: Project Home (nonprofit), using Dane County Community Development Block Grant funds
record.summary: Grant-funded minor home repairs and accessibility work for income-qualified homeowners in Dane County, outside the City of Madison.
record.benefit: Necessary repairs (health-and-safety items and code violations prioritised) performed by Project Home staff. A grant -- no repayment for the Dane County program (unlike the Sun Prairie deferred-loan version).

steps: Confirm your home is in a participating Dane County municipality (not the City of Madison), you own and occupy it, and your income is within the chart.
Download and submit the PDF application, or call the Home Repair Division.
Project Home performs a Housing Quality Standards inspection; only items that fail HQS are eligible to be repaired.

of._sourceText: Your home must be located in a participating municipality in Dane County
Homes in the following municipalities are not eligible: City of Madison (see City of Madison Minor Home Repair Program)
You must own and live in your home.

Your total gross household income cannot exceed 80% of the Dane County Median Income. [table] Household Size 1 = $74,800 ... (identical to HUD 80% AMI Low Income limits, and to the Madison CDA public-housing column)
Your home cannot exceed 95% of the Dane County Median Purchase Price ... Single family home: $397,000 Duplex: $508,000
The property cannot be currently on the market ... or be put on the market ... within the next twelve (12) months. The property cannot be in foreclosure ...

factsNeeded.sourceText: home cannot exceed 95% of the Dane County Median Purchase Price ($397,000 single family / $508,000 duplex) -- an asset-style test on the home's value, distinct from income
cannot be currently/soon on the market to be sold, or in/going into foreclosure within 12 months

unencodable: The HQS inspection outcome -- only items that fail Housing Quality Standards are eligible to be repaired; health/safety and code violations prioritised. Determines what work is done, not strictly who is eligible, but shapes whether applying is worthwhile.
'participating municipality' -- not every Dane County town participates; the list is not on the page.
New construction and remodeling are excluded.

hops: minor-home-repair/ -- describes three geographically distinct programs (City of Madison, Dane County, Sun Prairie), each with an 'Eligibility Requirements & Income Chart' link
-> .../dane-county-minor-eligibilty-income-chart/ -- the Dane County program's rule + the size-scoped income table

scopeColocated.figure: $74,800 (household size 1) / '80% of the Dane County Median Income'
scopeColocated.scopeLocation: The income chart page states '80% of the Dane County Median Income' immediately above a 'Household Size | Maximum Annual Gross Income' table. Clean. But note the SAME figure appears on THREE pages in this pilot (here, Madison CDA public housing, and implicitly HUD's dataset) each described differently ('80% Dane County Median Income' vs 'federal income limits' vs 'Low Income'), so a reader could fail to recognise them as the same limit.
Stated with its scope ('95% of the Dane County Median Purchase Price', single family vs duplex) in the same bullet.

cost.notes: 2 fetches + 1 search. The 'three programs on one page, each with its own chart link' structure meant one wrong click was possible; the Dane County chart URL had a typo in the site's own slug ('eligibilty').

surprises: A repair program with an asset test (home value <= $397k) and a 'not trying to sell' test -- eligibility conditions that are neither income, geography, nor a categorical status, and that no current fact key resembles. The corpus keeps turning up condition types the vocabulary has no shape for.
